newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish fund sells Espebepe shares.
newsitem.headline: Polish fund sells Espebepe shares.

text.p: The Polish Private Equity Fund I (PPEF I) sold for an undisclosed amount 47,042 shares of the construction company Espebepe SA, which is threatened with bankruptcy, the fund's deputy president said on Tuesday.
Ryszard Kruk told Reuters that after the transaction the fund still held 105,968 shares of Espebepe, giving it 4.69 percent of shareholder votes.

At the Tuesday bourse session Espebepe traded at 3.5 zlotys per share after it had plunged to 3.15 zlotys from 5.75 zlotys at the end of October when it announced it could go bankrupt if its creditors did not agree to a debt write-off. @
The other major shareholders of Espebepe are The Polish Private Equity Fund II, Bank Gdanski, Bel Leasing Ltd and the Polish American Enterprise Fund.
Espebepe made a net loss of 10.13 million zlotys over the first three quarters this year against a 17.6-million-zloty loss for all of 1995.
